definition.en: Captures human instructions and AI agent operations, including MCP tool calls, resource access, generation, delegation, evaluation, approvals and governance outcomes. Version 0.10.0 adds a robotics and physical-AI module for robots, hybrid AI and swarms: one verb per memory-record type, telemetry windows (pose, navigation, sensor), and provenance extensions that let any statement be verified against its signed source record. Concepts are aligned with the I2IDL Glossary of Digital Learning (v0.0.93) where a match exists.
Human or system issued an instruction to an AI agent to perform a task.
AI agent produced a plan or chain of steps prior to execution.
AI agent handed off a subtask to another agent.
AI agent called a tool (e.g., via the MCP tools interface) with parameters.
AI agent retrieved context from a resource (file, database, API, knowledge base).
AI agent persisted or updated content in a resource.
AI agent produced an output (text, code, image, report).
AI agent assessed content or results against criteria or policy.
Human or supervising agent approved a plan or output.
Human or supervising agent rejected a plan or output.
Agent or human ended a run or session before completion.
A software agent that acts on behalf of a human or another agent.
A person who instructs, supervises or approves agent work.
A callable capability, such as an MCP tool server.
A file, database table, API endpoint or other data source.
An instruction or prompt given to a model.
An AI model.
One model session or agent run.
A unit of work an agent was asked to do.
A rule or policy that constrains agent behavior.
Identifier of the MCP server involved.
Identifier of the MCP client involved.
MCP transport: stdio, http or sse.
Name of the tool invoked.
Parameters passed to the tool (redact as needed).
Identifier of the model used.
Generation parameters (temperature, top_p, ...).
Number of input tokens.
Number of output tokens.
Elapsed time in milliseconds.
Cost of the operation, if known.
URI of the resource read or written.
Hash of the resource content.
Version of the resource.
Policies applied to the operation.
Risk score assigned to the operation.
Whether the operation was flagged as anomalous, with a reason.
Session identifier for traceability.
Run identifier for traceability.
Identifier of the parent run.
Distributed trace identifier.
A robot or AI agent sensed something outside or inside its own body (camera, range sensor, battery, temperature).
An agent reasoned without committing to act: a plan, prediction, question or interpretation.
An agent committed to act, or not to act.
An agent did something in the world or in software; the result carries the outcome.
An agent sent or received a message to or from another agent or a person.
An agent drew a conclusion from experience that is meant to change its future behavior.
An operator issued a rule that constrains agent or swarm behavior.
The memory server recorded a system fact (startup, key change, integrity result).
One signed, hash-chained memory record from a robot or AI agent, identified by agent and sequence number.
A governed group of robots and agents with an appointed hub, used as a grouping context.
A named physical or logical location where a record was made.
contextAgents relevantType: an agent the record involved (sender, receiver, observed peer).
contextAgents relevantType: the hub that relayed the record to the memory server.
The record's per-agent sequence number (integer >= 1).
SHA-256 of the signed record (lowercase hex). Verify against the memory server.
Hash of the agent's previous record (hash chain).
SHA-256 of the record payload. The payload itself is not exported by default.
The author's Ed25519 signature over the record (hex).
The Holocron record type: communication, thought, decision, action, event, perception, lesson, policy or system.
The record's tags, e.g. telemetry, internal.
Links to other records by role, e.g. {"because": "robot-1:41"}. Values are agent:seq strings or lists of them.
When the memory server accepted the record (ISO 8601).
Version of the record-to-statement mapping. Statement ids are derived per mapping version.
What the actor is: robot, ai-agent, relay or human.
The actor's software or firmware version string.
How an action ended: success, partial, reflex_stop, stuck, abandoned or failed. result.success is true only for success.
A periodic sensor window: pose, navigation or sensor samples. Large windows are exported as a summary (samples_count, truncated: true).
A Holocron `perception` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `thought` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `decision` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `action` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `communication` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `event` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `lesson` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `policy` record exported as a statement.
A Holocron `system` record exported as a statement.
A perception record tagged telemetry whose payload is a pose window.
A perception record tagged telemetry whose payload is a navigation window.
A perception record tagged telemetry whose payload is a sensor window.
